facts.label: Admission and aid for international students (Harvard)

value.text: Admission decisions are made without regard to whether an applicant has applied for financial aid. Harvard meets each student's demonstrated need, and its aid policies are the same for all applicants, whatever their nationality or citizenship.

facts.label: Admission and aid for international students (MIT)

value.text: MIT is need-blind in admission and meets the full need of all undergraduates, domestic and international.

facts.label: Admission and aid for international students (Yale)

value.text: International applicants are considered without regard to their ability to pay, and Yale meets 100% of every family's demonstrated financial need.

facts.label: Admission and aid for international students (Princeton)

value.text: Admission is need-blind for international students, and Princeton meets the full need of every admitted international student with grants. Princeton gives no academic or athletic merit scholarships.

facts.label: Admission and aid for international students (Dartmouth)

value.text: Dartmouth has been need-blind for all international citizens since the Class of 2026, and meets the demonstrated need of every admitted student, including students from other countries.

facts.label: Admission and aid for international students (Brown)

value.text: Brown is need-blind for international students from the Class of 2029, which started in autumn 2025, and meets full demonstrated need for admitted students who applied for aid when they applied for admission.

facts.label: Admission and aid for international students (Amherst)

value.text: Amherst is need-blind for all applicants, domestic and international, and meets 100% of calculated need for every admitted international student who applies for aid.

facts.label: Admission and aid for international students (Bowdoin)

value.text: Bowdoin is need-blind for international students and meets the full calculated need of every admitted student, with no loans.

facts.label: Admission and aid for international students (Williams)

value.text: Williams is need-aware for international applicants, which means the ability to pay can affect admission. Its aid awards meet 100% of demonstrated need for all four years.

facts.label: Admission and aid for international students (Swarthmore)

value.text: Admission is need-aware for international citizens. For an admitted student who applied for aid, Swarthmore meets 100% of institutionally determined need, without loans.

facts.label: Admission and aid for international students (Stanford)

value.text: Stanford is need-aware for international applicants: a request for aid is a factor in the admission decision. It meets the full need of all admitted students, regardless of citizenship.

facts.label: Admission and aid for international students (Columbia)

facts.label: Admission and aid for international students (Penn)

facts.label: Student visa terms for Bangladeshi citizens

value.text: For Bangladeshi citizens, the F-1 visa has no issuance fee, allows multiple entries and can be valid for up to 60 months.

facts.label: Where to apply for the student visa

value.text: Book your visa interview at a US Embassy or Consulate in your country of nationality or residence. Applying on the basis of residence means showing that you live there.

facts.label: What to bring to the visa interview

value.text: A passport valid for at least six months beyond your stay, the DS-160 confirmation page, the fee receipt, a photo if the upload failed, and your I-20. The officer may also ask for academic records, test scores, evidence that you will leave the USA after your studies, and proof of how you will pay.

facts.where: Sections: Required documentation and Additional documentation may be required

facts.label: In-person visa interviews

value.text: Since 1 October 2025, most visa applicants, student visa applicants included, generally need an in-person interview with a consular officer.

facts.where: Paragraphs on who needs an interview
facts.note: Student visas are not among the exceptions.

value.text: An officer refuses a visa under section 214(b) when not satisfied that you qualify, including that you have ties, such as a job, a home or family, that will make you leave the USA after your stay. The refusal is for that application only. You can apply again with a new form, a new fee and a new interview, and should show what has changed. There is no appeal.

facts.label: A refusal under section 221(g)

value.text: A refusal under section 221(g) means the application is incomplete or needs administrative processing. You have one year to send what is missing; after that you must apply and pay again.

facts.note: The State Department counts it as a refusal, even while the checks continue.

facts.label: What visitors cannot bring into the US Embassy in Dhaka

value.text: Cameras, mobile phones, laptops and other small electronic devices, smart watches and other wearables, and luggage. The embassy has no storage for visitors' belongings.

facts.label: When to arrive at the US Embassy in Dhaka

value.text: Arrive about 15 minutes before your appointment.

facts.note: The page also covers other services, whose rules differ.

facts.label: Who issues the I-20

value.text: Only a school approved by the Student and Exchange Visitor Program can issue the I-20 that a student visa needs.

facts.where: Section: Acceptance at a SEVP-approved school

facts.label: Visa brokers and false documents

value.text: The US Embassy in Dhaka says applicants do not need a visa broker and can apply online themselves. False information or documents can lead to a refusal and to an ineligibility that prevents future travel to the USA.

facts.where: Opening paragraphs, quoting the embassy's statement of 20 January 2023

value.text: Since 21 January 2026, a Bangladeshi citizen found eligible for a B-1 or B-2 visitor visa must post a bond of USD 10,000, 15,000 or 20,000, set at the interview. The rule covers B-1 and B-2 visitor visas only.

facts.label: How long a student may stay: the 2026 rule

value.text: A rule published in July 2026 would give F-1 students a fixed admission period of up to four years instead of duration of status. A federal court paused it on 14 September 2026, so the existing system still applies for now.

facts.note: The government may appeal, so this can change.

facts.label: How Texas State University reads Bangladeshi HSC marks

value.text: Marks of 60 to 100 count as A, 4 points; 45 to 59 as B, 3 points; 33 to 44 as C, 2 points; 0 to 32 as F, 0 points.

facts.label: How Western Kentucky University reads Bangladeshi marks

value.text: Marks of 60 to 100 count as A, 50 to 59 as B, 35 to 49 as C and 0 to 34 as F.

facts.note: Western Kentucky's own document, which carries no date. Other universities may read marks differently.

facts.label: Reporting a GPA on a scale the Common App does not list

value.text: If your school uses a GPA scale that is not among the options, leave the cumulative GPA field blank, because it is not required, and explain your school's grading in Additional Information.
